description: Execution-depth playbook for approved FinOps tactics. This is prescription/reference material only and must never be used as customer source evidence.

entries.activity_goal: Create enforceable tag and allocation rules that make cloud spend attributable to accountable teams, products, services, or cost centers.
when_to_use: Source evidence shows weak or inconsistent tagging
Allocation or showback depends on manual cleanup
Policy exists but enforcement is missing
when_not_to_use: The locked findings show mature tag compliance with automated enforcement
The immediate issue is dashboard access rather than allocation quality
implementation_activities: Define mandatory tag keys and allowed values
Deploy policy-as-code checks in cloud accounts and CI/CD
Report compliance by team and service
acceptance_criteria: Non-compliant resources are visible by owner
New deployments are checked before release
Exceptions have an accountable owner and expiry
risks_and_controls: Enforcement can break deployments; start with audit mode and time-boxed exceptions

entries.activity_goal: Give engineering teams usable cost visibility for the services they influence so cost decisions move closer to the work.
when_to_use: Cost data is visible only to finance or administrators
Teams lack self-service dashboards
Monthly invoice review is the main cost feedback loop
when_not_to_use: Dashboards already show team-owned cost with active engineering usage
The main blocker is allocation data quality rather than dashboard access
prerequisite_evidence: Billing export or cost API access
implementation_activities: Publish cost by service, owner, environment, and trend
Route dashboard access to engineering managers and service owners
acceptance_criteria: Each team can see its own cloud cost
Dashboard data refresh cadence is documented
Cost view includes allocation owner or service
risks_and_controls: Raw spend without context creates noise; include ownership, trends, and actionable drivers

entries.activity_goal: Normalize multi-provider cost data so reporting, allocation, and governance use a common cost language.
when_to_use: Cost views are split across providers, accounts, or tools
Hybrid or multi-cloud scope prevents consolidated reporting
Procurement or compliance needs consistent reporting
when_not_to_use: The assessed scope is single-provider and not fragmented
Basic billing export is missing and must be established first
implementation_activities: Choose a normalization model or FOCUS-compatible schema
Map accounts to owners and business units
acceptance_criteria: Major providers appear in one reporting view
Reporting users can compare provider cost consistently
risks_and_controls: Normalization can hide provider nuance; keep provider-specific fields available for drilldown

entries.activity_goal: Detect cost anomalies quickly and route them to accountable owners before monthly reporting exposes the issue late.
when_to_use: Cost spikes are discovered late
Anomaly detection or alert routing is absent
Budget thresholds exist but ownership response is unclear
when_not_to_use: Anomaly alerts already route to owners with documented resolution
The source has no cost data or owner mapping to support alert design
implementation_activities: Define anomaly thresholds by service and team
Route alerts to service owners and finance
Create triage workflow and escalation rules
risks_and_controls: Alert fatigue reduces trust; start with material thresholds and tune after review

entries.activity_goal: Create a controlled commitment purchasing process for stable usage while avoiding stranded commitments.
when_to_use: Stable on-demand usage exists without commitment strategy
Commitment coverage or utilization is unknown
Procurement decisions are not tied to usage forecasts
when_not_to_use: Usage is volatile and no baseline can be trusted
The locked findings already show healthy commitment coverage and utilization
implementation_activities: Review purchase risk with finance and engineering
acceptance_criteria: Purchase candidates trace to stable usage
risks_and_controls: Over-commitment creates waste; start conservative and expand only after utilization evidence

entries.activity_goal: Turn utilization evidence into controlled right-sizing actions that preserve reliability while reducing over-provisioning.
when_to_use: Low utilization or over-provisioning is evidenced
Right-sizing recommendations are not reviewed
Production changes lack performance validation
when_not_to_use: No utilization data exists
The gap is commitment pricing rather than resource sizing
prerequisite_evidence: CPU, memory, storage, or network utilization
implementation_activities: Rank right-sizing candidates by materiality and risk
Track accepted, rejected, and deferred recommendations
risks_and_controls: Aggressive downsizing can harm performance; require workload validation and rollback path

entries.activity_goal: Remove idle, orphaned, and expired resources through governed lifecycle controls rather than ad hoc cleanup campaigns.
when_to_use: Orphaned or idle resources are evidenced
Dev/test environments run without schedules
Ownership or expiry metadata is missing
when_not_to_use: Resource inventory and lifecycle automation are already operating
The main issue is pricing strategy rather than waste
acceptance_criteria: Deleted resources have approval or retention logic
risks_and_controls: Cleanup can remove needed assets; use soft-delete, owner approval, and recovery windows

entries.activity_goal: Use spot or preemptible capacity only for workloads that can tolerate interruption and retry safely.
when_to_use: Fault-tolerant workloads are identified but not using spot/preemptible capacity
Batch, CI/CD, or test workloads run on on-demand capacity
Interruption handling can be designed
when_not_to_use: Workloads are latency-sensitive, stateful, or lack retry design
No workload eligibility evidence exists
risks_and_controls: Spot interruption can disrupt service; limit to eligible workloads and test failure paths

entries.activity_goal: Control storage growth and tiering through documented lifecycle policies and access-pattern evidence.
when_to_use: Storage lifecycle management is absent
Snapshots or retained data create waste
Access patterns support tiering decisions
when_not_to_use: Storage access patterns are unknown
Retention requirements prevent lifecycle automation
implementation_activities: Classify storage by owner and access pattern
risks_and_controls: Aggressive tiering can harm access; validate access patterns and compliance constraints first

entries.activity_goal: Define and enforce the financial guardrails that make cloud spend governable without turning governance into a manual bottleneck.
when_to_use: Cloud financial policy is missing or fragmented
Spend approvals, tags, budgets, or exceptions are unclear
Policy intent exists but enforcement is weak
when_not_to_use: The issue is only architecture cost estimation
Policy exists and the gap is cultural adoption or dashboard usage
acceptance_criteria: Engineering has a clear path to compliant provisioning
risks_and_controls: Overly strict policy slows delivery; use guardrails and automated feedback before hard gates

entries.activity_goal: Bring cloud account creation under governed provisioning so ownership, billing, and baseline controls are applied by default.
when_to_use: Shadow accounts or unmanaged subscriptions are evidenced
Account ownership is unclear
New accounts bypass baseline cost controls
when_not_to_use: Account governance is mature and the issue is resource-level waste
No cloud account structure evidence exists
acceptance_criteria: New accounts are provisioned through the approved workflow
risks_and_controls: Unmanaged accounts may host production workloads; migrate with owners instead of terminating abruptly

entries.activity_goal: Turn budgets from passive reports into accountable thresholds with defined response paths.
when_to_use: Budget overruns are tolerated
Alerts exist but escalation is unclear
Teams are not accountable for budget variance
when_not_to_use: No budget model exists yet
Production hard stops would create unacceptable service risk
implementation_activities: Use hard controls only for safe non-production scopes
risks_and_controls: Hard stops can disrupt service; use progressive controls and production-safe escalation

entries.activity_goal: Measure FinOps by operational outcomes instead of activity volume, meetings, or vanity metrics.
when_to_use: FinOps activity exists but outcomes are unclear
KPIs track reporting effort rather than savings, waste, or unit economics
Continuous improvement is not evidenced
when_not_to_use: No baseline metrics exist at all
The locked findings do not show outcome-tracking weakness
implementation_activities: Link actions to savings, waste, coverage, or unit economics
acceptance_criteria: Activity-only metrics no longer drive status
risks_and_controls: Outcome targets without reliable baselines damage trust; validate baseline before setting targets

entries.activity_goal: Review migrated or legacy workloads for cloud-native cost and architecture improvements after the initial move.
when_to_use: Lift-and-shift patterns are evidenced
Migrated workloads are not right-sized or modernized
Container/serverless optimization is absent
when_not_to_use: Workloads are already optimized cloud-native services
No architecture or workload inventory exists
implementation_activities: Rank migrated workloads by cost and risk
Sequence changes by value and operational risk
risks_and_controls: Modernization can add delivery risk; prioritize stable high-cost workloads and require rollback plans

entries.activity_goal: Make cost visible before architecture and infrastructure decisions are approved.
when_to_use: Architecture decisions are cost-blind
IaC or design reviews lack cost estimates
New deployments do not show cost impact before approval
when_not_to_use: Architecture reviews already require cost estimates
The issue is runtime waste after deployment rather than design-time visibility
implementation_activities: Add cost section to design documents
Integrate cost estimates into IaC pull requests
Track decisions with material cost impact
acceptance_criteria: Material architecture decisions include cost estimates
IaC changes show expected cost impact
risks_and_controls: Estimates are directional; use them for decision quality, not exact forecasts

entries.activity_goal: Add cost guardrails to autoscaling so scale events remain reliable and financially bounded.
when_to_use: Autoscaling lacks limits or cost guardrails
Runaway scaling risk is evidenced
Thresholds and circuit breakers are absent
when_not_to_use: No autoscaling is used or evidenced
The issue is static over-provisioning rather than scaling behavior
risks_and_controls: Cost limits can affect availability; balance guardrails with service reliability requirements

entries.activity_goal: Give engineering teams cost accountability together with the visibility and authority needed to act.
when_to_use: Cost is treated as finance-only or IT-only
Engineering teams lack accountability for spend
Teams cannot see or influence their service cost
when_not_to_use: Engineering already owns cost outcomes with dashboards and decision rights
The issue is financial policy rather than team ownership
implementation_activities: Assign cost ownership by service or team
Add cost review to engineering cadence
acceptance_criteria: Cost is reviewed in engineering cadence
risks_and_controls: Accountability without control creates blame; pair expectations with tooling and support

entries.activity_goal: Create a working cadence between finance, engineering, and business stakeholders so cloud cost decisions are shared.
when_to_use: Finance and engineering operate separately
FinOps decisions lack cross-functional participation
Cost questions are lost between teams
when_not_to_use: A cross-functional cadence already operates with decisions and owners
The gap is purely technical cost visibility
acceptance_criteria: Finance and engineering use the same cost view
risks_and_controls: Meetings without decisions become theater; require inputs, outputs, and action tracking

entries.activity_goal: Turn executive interest in FinOps into funded ownership, mandate, and measurable operating capacity.
when_to_use: FinOps sponsorship is aspirational
No funded team or mandate exists
Investment case for tooling or headcount is missing
when_not_to_use: A funded FinOps function with executive mandate already exists
Evidence is too weak to estimate investment need
implementation_activities: Build investment case from verified spend and gaps
acceptance_criteria: Executive sponsor is named by role
Funding or capacity decision is made
risks_and_controls: Inflated savings claims reduce credibility; base the case on verified evidence and conservative assumptions

entries.activity_goal: Use cost incidents and overruns as system-learning events rather than blame events.
when_to_use: Cost management is blame-oriented
Teams avoid surfacing cost issues
Cost incidents lack learning reviews
when_not_to_use: No evidence of blame culture or cost incident behavior exists
The problem is missing visibility rather than review culture
risks_and_controls: Blameless language without leadership behavior will fail; leaders must model the expected response

entries.activity_goal: Make token, model, API, and inference spend attributable to accountable products, teams, use cases, customers, and environments.
when_to_use: AI costs are visible only as platform or provider totals
Token/API/model usage has no product or owner allocation
AI pilots or production apps generate spend without accountable cost dimensions
when_not_to_use: AI spend is already allocated to owners and unit economics
The source has no evidence of AI/API/model usage
prerequisite_evidence: Request metadata or AI gateway logs
implementation_activities: Instrument AI requests with owner and use-case metadata
Publish token and model spend dashboards
Review unallocated AI spend each month
acceptance_criteria: AI spend is reportable by owner and use case
Cost owners review AI spend cadence
risks_and_controls: Avoid storing sensitive prompts or personal data; meter cost metadata without unnecessary content capture

entries.activity_goal: Control GenAI unit cost by routing work to appropriate models and managing context, caching, batching, and retry behavior.
when_to_use: Premium models are used without task-based justification
Prompt/context growth is uncontrolled
Retries, agent loops, or RAG retrieval inflate token cost
when_not_to_use: Model selection is already governed by cost-quality evaluations
Quality or risk requirements explicitly justify premium model use
implementation_activities: Define model tiers by task complexity and risk
Measure cache hit rate and retry volume
risks_and_controls: Lower-cost routing can reduce output quality; use evaluation thresholds and exception paths for high-risk tasks

entries.activity_goal: Govern AI consumption with budgets, alerts, approvals, and value metrics so adoption does not outpace financial accountability.
when_to_use: AI usage grows without budgets or quotas
AI spend anomalies or runaway retries are not detected
AI success is measured by activity rather than value per outcome
when_not_to_use: No AI consumption is evidenced
The immediate blocker is basic attribution rather than budget or value governance
implementation_activities: Set AI budgets and quota thresholds
Route spend and token anomaly alerts to owners
Define approval rules for premium model expansion
Review low-value or high-cost use cases for redesign
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly alerts route to accountable teams
Cost per outcome is reviewed for material use cases
risks_and_controls: Value metrics can become vanity metrics; tie them to verified workflows, business outcomes, and owner decisions
